title: Connectivity of the derived tensor product
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, with small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $\Lambda_T$ be its constant sheaf of rings [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Work in the derived category $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor product [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $A,B\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Assume that $A$ has tor amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], meaning that $\mathcal H^i(A\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M)=0$ for every sheaf $\mathcal M$ of $\Lambda_T$-modules placed in degree zero and every $i<a$. If $\mathcal H^i(B)=0$ for every $i<b$, then
$$
\mathcal H^i(A\kunotimes{\Lambda}B)=0\qquad(i<a+b).
$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f1m] to $A$ with its assumed tor-amplitude bound $[a,\infty)$. It gives a representing cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_T$-modules that is K-flat, has flat terms, and satisfies $P^p=0$ for $p<a$. Only the model assertion is needed, not the additional assertion about pullbacks. This is exactly where the tor-amplitude hypothesis, absent from the imported statement, is used.

Choose a representing complex $C^\bullet$ for $B$ using [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and form $L^\bullet=\tau_{\ge b}C^\bullet$ as in [def-kun-truncations]. Explicitly, $L^q=0$ for $q<b$, $L^b=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{b-1})$, and $L^q=C^q$ for $q>b$. The quotient map $C^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ induces the identity on $\ker(d_C^b)/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{b-1})$ in degree $b$; in degree $b+1$ its incoming image is still $\operatorname{im}(d_C^b)$, and all higher differentials are unchanged. Thus it induces isomorphisms on cohomology in degrees at least $b$. Below $b$, the source cohomology is zero by hypothesis and the target terms are zero. The map is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, hence becomes an isomorphism in the localization defining the derived category. Consequently $L^\bullet$ represents $B$ and is supported in degrees at least $b$. No flatness or K-flatness of $L^\bullet$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), cochain canonical lower truncation and its cohomology

proof.text: Use $P^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ as the representing complexes of $A$ and $B$. In [def-kun-derived-tensor] the K-flat replacement of the first representing complex can now be the identity $P^\bullet\to P^\bullet$. Its defining formula therefore computes $A\kunotimes{\Lambda}B$ as $Q(P^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda L^\bullet)$, where $Q$ is localization. This computation requires K-flatness only of the first factor, already supplied in step 1.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), K-flat model construction immediately preceding the definition

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the degree $i$ term of $P^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda L^\bullet$ is $\bigoplus_{p+q=i}P^p\otimes_{\Lambda_T}L^q$. If $i<a+b$ and $p+q=i$, the simultaneous inequalities $p\ge a$ and $q\ge b$ are impossible. Thus either $P^p=0$ or $L^q=0$, so each tensor summand is zero and their direct sum is zero. It follows that this total complex has zero terms, and hence zero cohomology, in every degree below $a+b$. The cohomology of its image under $Q$ is the cohomology of this representing complex by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Combined with step 3 this proves the required vanishing. The argument uses actual termwise support and involves no spectral-sequence convergence claim.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), direct-sum totalization formula, applied to tensor complexes as in Tag 06YM

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported lower bound from cohomological connectivity alone is false, even for finite coefficients. Corrected the first-factor hypothesis to tor amplitude in [a,infinity), which is available in the intended Stacks 0F1J flat-tail argument. Replaced the wrongly indexed Tor spectral sequence by four steps using existing K-flat model and truncation nodes; no new nodes. Full counterexample, source comparison, downstream implication, search results and citation audit are in report.md.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the K-flat-model opening and final lower-bound conclusion of the master blueprint proof. The intermediate Tor spectral sequence with abutment degree p+q is false in cohomological indexing: Tor_p contributes in degree -p. Its replacement is the lower Tor-amplitude model of Stacks 0F1M, good truncation of the other factor and the direct-sum support calculation. The main-20261015 statement repeats the same error; the replacement stays within the ordinary Kunneth unit and its Stacks 0F1J reduction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-9343e592a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full, all 8 cited node statements, the citer lem-kun-0f1j (statement and all 4 steps), the unit record, the master and main-20261015 blueprint texts (statement and proof identical in both), and Stacks 0F1M (sites-cohomology l.12472) and 0F1J (etale-cohomology proof l.20736-20756). The imported statement is false; I checked the counterexample myself: over Z/4, Z/2 derived-tensor Z/2 has H^{-k}=Z/2 for every k>=0. The blueprint proof also grades Tor_p in degree +p instead of -p (E7). The report names the change under its own source-error heading. The corrected hypothesis (A has tor amplitude in [a,inf)) is what 0F1J provides for its tail E''=sigma_{>=N+1}E. That tail is K-flat (kernel of a termwise-split map onto a bounded flat complex), supported in degrees >=N+1, and stable under pullback by 0F1M. The new hypothesis implies the old one on A by testing with Lambda_T. The item is not a target and not its unit's statement. Steps: (1) lem-kun-0f1m gives a K-flat complex of flat modules with P^p=0 for p<a, on the same unit, with no cycle. (2) The quotient onto the canonical truncation tau_{>=b} is a quasi-isomorphism; I re-checked the kernel/cokernel calculation. (3) The derived tensor definition allows the identity K-flat model for the first factor. (4) In the total tensor complex every summand in degree <a+b is zero, so no spectral sequence is needed. All three elementary markings are justified, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. There are no new nodes. The duplicate search found only lem-kun-integral-derived-tensor-bounded-torsion (Z coefficients, bound r<a+b-1), which is a different statement. The coefficient category is ordinary Lambda_T-module sheaves on the small etale site, matching the citer. No SGA source, no tool_uses, no fixes. The maintainer should record the statement correction in HUMAN.md and the ledger. The future split of lem-kun-0f1j must justify the tor-amplitude hypothesis for p^{-1}E''.
